subject: Sev2: BrightLeaf hosted API p95/p99 latency spike — batching-induced queue accumulation
messages:
From: Kevin Liu <kevin@brightleaf.health>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:23 -0800
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 — hosted API — urgent

Hi Sean,

We started seeing a pronounced increase in p95 and p99 for our inference calls to the hosted API around 08:45 PST this morning. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~2.6s; error rate crept from 0.05% to ~0.9%. Throughput nominal, but tail latency is killing our UX.

We've attached a small sample of request traces and one server-side error cluster. Can you help triage? We're seeing this across two regions (us-west-2, us-east-1). Our product team is on standby.

Attachments: brightleaf-error-sample-20280210.log

- Kevin
Kevin Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLeaf Health
kevin@brightleaf.health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:58:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — hosted API — urgent

Investigating now — early triage notes below.

What I see in ops telemetry (08:30–09:20 PST):
- Steady arrival rate per customer, but a spike in per-instance queue depth at the batcher layer starting 08:43.
- Batcher stickiness: requests are accumulating into in-flight batches longer than the configured batching window (~15ms) due to a sudden surge in many very short requests (avg token < 16). Instead of more small batches, we observed a small number of oversized batches that then serialized execution and inflated p95/p99.
- KV-cache misses increased marginally (prefix variations) which amplified execution time for some hot keys.

Attached: p95-trend-20280210-0213.png and a CSV snapshot of the request bucket at 08:50.

Immediate hypothesis: a workload pattern shift produced atypical microbursts of short-lived requests that cause batching windows to coalesce, creating deep per-worker queues. This matches BrightLeaf's symptom (tails up, throughput steady).

Planned mitigations (initial, non-disruptive):
1) Lower batching window from 15ms -> 6ms in the affected host-pool for BrightLeaf routes (trial).
2) Add transient request prioritization for interactive routes (reduce waiting time for single-user requests).
3) Hot-key prefix warmup to reduce KV-cache miss cost.

I will run the window change in canary now and report back within 30 minutes. If this helps we can roll to all host-pools and then consider a longer-term routing fix (workload-aware batching thresholds).

—Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 10:22:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — hosted API — urgent

Update: canary applied — initial effect positive.

What changed: batching window to 6ms on the canary subset of hosts serving BrightLeaf. Observed within 5 minutes:
- p95 dropped from 1.2s -> ~320ms on canary hosts; p99 also materially improved.
- Overall error rate on canary fell to baseline.

Caveats:
- The canary hosts showed slightly higher CPU overhead (more smaller batches), but within service limits.
- We still see a subset (~8%) of requests with elevated latency tied to KV misses.

Next steps:
- Promote window change to remaining hosts for BrightLeaf (15m maintenance run)
- Kick off a short-lived cache-key reconciliation job to reduce KV misses
- Add an automated guard to adapt batching window by observed short-request microburst patterns (post-mortem work)

Attaching the p95 screenshot and request bucket snapshot.

—Marissa

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Kevin — quick update and mitigation ask:

We have identified batching-window coalescence as the dominant contributor to tail latency. Marissa applied a canary change and it improved tail latency materially on those hosts. Our recommended short-term plan to restore your UX ASAP:

1) Allow Redwood to promote batching-window change across your route (15-minute rolling change, no downtime).
2) Optionally, we can failover your traffic to a dedicated host-pool with slightly higher concurrency to blunt any future microburst effects — this would be a quick config change but may affect billing tier (I’ll run cost delta separately).

If you approve step 1 I’ll schedule promotion immediately; we can do step 2 after we stabilize.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a root-cause post-mortem and a longer-term adaptive batching control.

—Grace O’Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — hosted API — urgent

Kevin — follow-up and exec note.

Summary:
- Root cause (short-term): transient workload microbursts of many short requests caused batching-window coalescence and per-worker queue depth growth. This serialized execution and inflated tail latency.
- Immediate remediation (done Friday): batching window reduced to 6ms for BrightLeaf routes across all host-pools; promoted canary to full POOL in ~15 minutes. p95 returned to ~280–350ms across both regions.
- Next steps (in progress): cache-key warmup job to address KV-cache misses; implement adaptive batching thresholds (Q2 milestone); monitoring alert refinement to auto-scale host-pool when queue-depth > threshold.

We've marked this Sev2, provided the timeline to your team, and Grace will follow up on the dedicated host-pool option and cost delta. We will publish a short post-mortem and the planned timeline for adaptive batching work.

If you want an immediate failover to a dedicated pool, we can schedule that this week; otherwise we believe the promoted change restores acceptable UX and the follow-up actions will reduce recurrence risk.

Thanks for your patience — we take this seriously. I'll escalate this internally as needed to ensure completion of the post-mortem and the adaptive controls.

—Sean Gallagher
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
